definitions.independence: The approving account is a human account, different from every account that authored a commit in this pull request. Approvals from machine accounts are counted separately and never satisfy this test. This does not establish organisational independence, a different reporting line, or absence of interest in the change.
definitions.attribution: Machine authorship is inferred from commit message trailers. Assisted-by and Co-authored-by are counted separately because projects that have reasoned about this have adopted the former and several explicitly forbid the latter for a machine.
definitions.attribution_no_signal: No machine-authorship trailer was found on the commit. This is an absence of evidence. It is not evidence that no machine was involved, and it must never be read or reported as a human-authored count.
definitions.seal: The detached signature in pack.sig covers every byte of this file: the coverage counts, the rows, these definitions, the not-visible register and the window, not only the chain. It establishes that the pack was produced by the holder of Falden's private key and has not been altered since. It is not a claim that the measurements are correct or that collection was complete. The chain over commit object identifiers is a separate guarantee: it lets the reader re-derive the commit population from their own clone without trusting Falden.
definitions.approval_covers_head: An approving review was submitted against the final commit of the pull request. The reviewed commit id is assigned by the forge and is not writable by the author.
definitions.not_a_finding: Every number here is a measurement of what the forge and the git objects show. None of it is a control finding, an audit opinion, or a statement that any control is deficient. That determination belongs to the customer's own second line.
definitions.not_the_attestor: Falden supplies the record. The customer's auditor signs. Falden is not the attestor.
definitions.permission_set: Collected on GitHub App permissions Metadata (read) and Pull requests (read). Contents was not requested. Repository Administration and the organisation audit log were not requested. Being exact about what that grant proves: Pull requests (read) is on its own sufficient to fetch a diff, so the permission list does not by itself prevent Falden reading source. What prevents it is the collector, which refuses the file-contents endpoint before a request is issued. That is a claim about our own behaviour, so the behaviour is recorded: every outbound request is listed under egress and sealed with the rest of this pack.
definitions.pseudonymity: People appear as stable pseudonyms of the form p_ followed by eight hex characters, computed as HMAC-SHA256 of the lowercased account name under a 32 byte salt. The salt is not in this pack and never leaves your organisation, so you can resolve any pseudonym to a real person and nobody else can. The same person carries the same label in every row and in every pack made with the same salt, which is what makes the population testable. Machine accounts are left in the clear: a bot is not a person, and which agent wrote a change is the finding. Under GDPR this is pseudonymisation and not anonymisation, because the salt exists and you hold it. Two things are passed through as recorded rather than rewritten, because both are evidence: branch names, which sometimes contain a person's name, and the prose of commit messages, which contains whatever the author typed. Identity trailers inside commit messages are rewritten; the surrounding text is not.

items: Whether the recorded witness commits remain reachable from the default branch. Under squash or rebase merging the pull request's commits are collapsed or rewritten on merge, so those exact objects may not exist in the branch history afterwards. Confirming reachability requires the commit-by-SHA endpoint, which returns file patches and is refused by the collector, so this is declared rather than tested.
File contents, diffs, and patches. Contents was not requested and the collector refuses the files endpoint.
Branch protection configuration and whether a required gate was configured. That is repository Administration, which was not requested.
Administrative overrides, required-check skips, and force pushes as a complete log. Those live on the organisation audit log, which was not requested. Bypass coverage is therefore partial.
Whether a review was substantive. An approval is recorded as an event; its depth is not observable from this permission set.
Any change that did not arrive through a pull request on an installed repository.
Any change authored by a model deployed inside the customer's perimeter that emits no trailer and commits under an undeclared identity.

egress.note: Every outbound request this collection issued, sealed with the rest of the pack. The file-contents endpoint is refused by the collector before a request is issued, and its absence here is checkable rather than asserted. This records what the collector did on this run and is verifiable against Falden's published source and verifier. It cannot prove how a differently built binary would behave, which is why the source is published and why the collector can be run inside the customer's own environment.

feat(ci): VAUD-020 — migration lock-safety gate (lock_timeout on new migrations)

New CI gate (scripts/check-migration-lock-safety.mjs + workflow) blocks newly-added Prisma migrations that take a table lock (ALTER TABLE / non-CONCURRENTLY CREATE INDEX / ADD CONSTRAINT) without SET lock_timeout, and any TRUNCATE CASCADE. Scoped to ADDED migration files (git diff --diff-filter=A), so the pre-existing 61 unsafe migrations aren't retroactively gated. Prisma-compatible by design: migrations run in a transaction where CONCURRENTLY is illegal, so the enforceable discipline is bounding the lock wait (lock_timeout), not CONCURRENTLY — which is why raw squawk defaults (verified: they flag every Prisma migration) don't fit. Satisfiable: add SET lock_timeout = '5s' at the top. CLI-tested: fails on lock-taking-without-timeout + TRUNCATE CASCADE, passes on lock_timeout-present + no-lock DDL.
